name: Derinkuyu Tuff Complex (Cappadocian Underground Cities)
region: Cappadocia, Central Anatolia (Derinkuyu/Malakopi; cluster including Kaymaklı/Anaku, Mazıköy, Özkonak, Koramaz Valley)
summary: Multi-level settlements cut into Cappadocian volcanic tuff: self-supporting voids holding a steady 8–13 °C climate, with wells, stores, kitchens, stables, and later churches, used as inherited village infrastructure and as refuge. A functional palimpsest — later use is documented; first-carving is not.
longevity_basis: Attested operational span of the mature complex as village infrastructure and refuge, from the Arab–Byzantine wars through abandonment in the 1923–24 population exchange. First-carving is archaeologically invisible in tuff (each enlargement destroys earlier surfaces) and may be Iron Age; that hypothesis is not entered as longevity.

claims.statement: Cappadocian volcanic tuff can be cut with simple tools yet is self-supporting once exposed, and holds a deep temperature of roughly 8–13 °C, making climate-controlled storage and shelter possible without continuous fuel

The visitor complex is a functional palimpsest: professional survey records five levels, ~55 m depth, and 3,786 m², against the tourism figures of 18 levels / 85 m / 20,000 people, and first-carving dates cannot be fixed because each enlargement destroys earlier surfaces

Refuge and worship are documented late functions, not proven original ones: Cappadocian Greek speakers called the tunnels καταφύγια, used them in 1909, and abandoned them in the 1923–24 exchange; no ancient Greek, Hittite, or Assyrian text names Derinkuyu

The type is regional, not unique: 200–360 artificial-cavity settlements are recorded across Cappadocia's tuff, several of them multi-level, so Derinkuyu is a deep type-case rather than a one-off monument

evidence.source: Heritage for People / University of Florence feature on Derinkuyu: tuff workability, visitor-route stratigraphy (stables uppermost; stores and kitchens; communal-religious spaces deepest), and self-supporting excavation.

Yamaç, A. and colleagues, survey of Cappadocian underground cities: Derinkuyu recorded at 1,880 m of tunnel, 489 stations, 3,786 m², described as five levels and 55 m deep; Mazıköy larger at 4,453 m².

Yamaç, A. (2023) survey of Koramaz Valley underground cities near Kayseri: Cappadocian subterranean complexes had diverse original functions (storage, agricultural cavities, refuges) with no single template.

Bixio, R. et al. (2023) Intended Use and Dating of Dovecotes — typology-based dating for Cappadocian rock-cut architecture; first-carving dates can rarely be fixed because later reuse overwrites earlier surfaces.
Dawkins, R. M. (1916) Modern Greek in Asia Minor, p. 16 — Cappadocian Greek καταφύγια; 1909 Adana-massacre refuge at Axo; local memory of Timurid-era use.

Xenophon, Anabasis 4.5.25 — underground houses with well-mouths, livestock ramps, stores and barley-wine; written from the 401 BCE march. Geography is Western Armenia (Erzurum–Aşkale), not Cappadocia. Documents the regional practice, not this site.
Paradeisopoulos, G. K. (2013) route analysis of Anabasis 4.5, Greek, Roman, and Byzantine Studies 53 — localizes Xenophon's underground villages to the Erzurum–Aşkale plain.
UNESCO World Heritage List, Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia (inscribed 1985, criteria i, iii, v, vii) — subterranean towns named as part of the troglodyte-village tradition.

notes: Added September 2026 from anthropology/findings/derinkuyu/. replication_regions=1 because the 200–360 Cappadocian complexes are one tuff tradition, not independent inventions; Xenophon's Armenian houses are a related practice in a different place. Attribution of first-carving is contested: Hittite and Phrygian origin claims remain hypotheses, and the Kültepe tablets ~75 km away are silent on city-scale underground complexes. Tourism figures (18 levels / 85 m / 20,000 people) are rejected in c2 rather than encoded. Boundary cut: this is the tuff-cut complex as climate-controlled, inheritable infrastructure — not Göreme cliff churches, not Hittite offering-pit ritual, not Anabasis 4.5.25.
